cannotDelete: This item is still in use and was not deleted

desc.ciTypes: Types for manually-registered ledger entities and the relation graph. Cloud resources (subnets / IPs / firewalls / CDN) and K8s resources (nodes / pods / volumes) are NOT registered here — collectors write them into their own tables with full attributes, so registering them again would create a second source of truth. Four types here is the designed boundary, not a gap.
desc.envs: Environment labels for assets (PROD / UAT / …). The code appears verbatim in APIs and MCP; the display name is only for humans.
desc.projects: Business projects, used for cost attribution and asset grouping.
desc.settings: Reminder cadence, audit retention, notification outlet. Set once and forget.
desc.statuses: Whether an asset still exists (in use / destroyed). This is what answers "is this machine still there".

dialog.envDesc: Environments tag assets and drive filtering.
dialog.projectDesc: Business projects drive cost attribution and asset grouping.
dialog.statusDesc: Lifecycle statuses are a configurable dictionary, not built in. Objects already tagged follow the change.

empty.ciTypes: With no CI types, assets cannot be categorised. This usually means the migration seed did not land.
empty.envs: With no environments, every page that filters by environment will return nothing.
empty.projects: With no business projects, all cost attribution falls into "unassigned".
empty.statuses: Without lifecycle statuses, in-use and destroyed assets cannot be told apart — destroyed machines keep counting toward cost.

field.codeChangeHint: ⚠️ The code is what the API and MCP actually use. Changing it breaks saved filter links.
field.codeHint: Uppercase, e.g. STAGING. It appears verbatim in APIs, MCP and filter parameters — do not change it after creation, as that is effectively a new one and every existing reference breaks.
field.label: Label
field.name: Name
field.nameEnHint: Optional. Shown in the English UI; falls back to the Chinese name when empty. This is data, not copy — an environment you create yourself will never be in the language pack.
field.scopeHint: domain / host / cert … Cannot be changed later: it decides which object type this status applies to
field.tagTypeHint: Use "Danger" for production — the point of the badge is to make it obvious what you are touching.

hint: Dictionaries for environments, projects and CI types. Every dropdown in the product draws from here — hard-coding an enum anywhere in the UI will drift from this.

settings.auditRetentionHint: ⚠️ 0 means never purge, not purge immediately — the two readings are opposite. With never-purge the audit table grows forever.
settings.remindDaysHint: Comma separated, e.g. 30,15,7,1 — one reminder on each of those days before expiry. Empty means no reminders.
settings.webhookHint: The global fallback outlet. A group bound to a specific task takes precedence.
